sections.title: A little seed. A whole world.
lines: Come along, little seed. Hills catch the rain. Water shapes a home. And one day, a forest grows. Let us follow the clues.

sections.title: The size of a hill
lines: First, raise the noise frequency. Broad hills become smaller ridges. The seed stays the same.

sections.title: A field is not its mesh
lines: More samples reveal the same landscape in finer detail.

sections.title: The mountain changes its coat
lines: Now raise the snow line. The mountain stays still; only its coat changes.

sections.title: Two rains, one beginning
lines: Give the same hills more rain. Water carries soil downhill, cutting some slopes and leaving sediment below.

sections.title: Where could the seed settle?
lines: Add moisture to the same land. The habitat map changes, opening different homes for life.

sections.title: The inside of a mountain
lines: Inside the mountain, density tells us where solid ground exists.

sections.title: An opening, and a surprise
lines: Widen the tunnel. A cave opens. Then add a pillar after cutting: the order changes what remains.

sections.title: A small edit stays small
lines: Carve one small pocket. Only nearby chunks need rebuilding; the distant landscape stays cached.

sections.title: The price of detail
lines: Finer voxels cost more work.

sections.title: Small pieces, more bookkeeping
lines: Smaller chunks change that tradeoff.

sections.title: Many ways to find a surface
lines: Marching Cubes finds the surface.

sections.title: A direction becomes a journey
lines: Turn the vector field. The same particles follow a new direction, revealing the invisible wind.

sections.title: Flow needs a little balance
lines: In this fluid study, dye follows the flow. Pressure correction reduces divergence. Watch the two versions side by side.

sections.title: A tree, written as a rule
lines: Repeat a branching rule. A simple line becomes a tree, one generation at a time.

sections.title: Open the branches
lines: Open the angle; spread the crown.

sections.title: Larger does not mean more
lines: With births switched off, trees grow larger, not more numerous.

sections.title: A forest has a history
lines: Now allow new seeds. The same starting forest becomes a growing population.

sections.title: Room to grow
lines: Crowding changes who can thrive.

sections.title: The path that comes and goes
lines: Here comes the tide. Follow the waterline as it climbs. A low path floods, and the route must change. As water retreats, the shore returns.

sections.title: A whole world of questions
lines: A little world, shaped by connected questions. Land, water, and life. These studies remain separate models. The next story begins with the rule you choose.
